subject: Proposal: hosted API commit increase and tier re-structure for Q3-Q4
messages:
From: Elise Thompson <elise@mercatorretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@mercatorretail.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Need options for committed throughput increase ahead of Q4 holiday

Jonas —

Quick note from our ops/eng team: we expect a sustained 1.8–2.2x uplift in API usage across inference and embeddings during the Sept–Dec window due to new personalization features. Our current monthly commit is 1.2B tokens; the elasticity we've seen on hosted is great but we need a predictable commit band and softer rate caps for short bursts.

Can Redwood provide a proposal for: 
- a 2x monthly commit (from 1.2B -> 2.4B) with a stepped discount on token rates,
- a larger burst buffer or soft-throttle window during peak hours, and
- a short-term pilot to validate latency at that scale (500 RPS sustained on text-generation).

Attached is a usage export and a short projection deck our SREs put together (usage_projection_Q3-Q4.xlsx). Happy to jump on a call this week — Rajiv and I are available on Friday afternoon PT.

Best,
Elise
Elise Thompson
Director, Platform Engineering
Mercator Retail

--
Attachment: usage_projection_Q3-Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet summary, 2 sheets)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elise Thompson <elise@mercatorretail.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@mercatorretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Need options for committed throughput increase ahead of Q4 holiday

Elise / Rajiv —

Thanks for the heads up and the projection — this is exactly the kind of lead time that makes for a smooth migration. I pulled together a concise proposal and a pricing summary (attached). High-level options: 

Option A — Stepped Commit (recommended)
- Monthly commit: 2.4B tokens (2x current)
- Token rate: 15% discount vs current rates on the first 2.4B; additional overage at current burst rates
- Burst pocket: 25% of monthly commit available as a soft buffer per week (auto-soft-throttle before hard rate limits)
- SLA: 99.9% availability for hosted API; priority provisioning during peak windows

Option B — Pilot + Gradual Step
- 3-month pilot with temporary bump to 1.8B for June–Aug, commit uplift to 2.4B starting Sept
- Lower initial commit commitment fee; conversion credit applied to first invoice if they convert to Option A

Operational notes:
- We recommend the prefix/KV caching and increased batching for your embedding-heavy endpoints; that will materially reduce per-token costs and latency.
- We'll provision a dedicated autoscale policy for the Sep–Dec window and add a Canary path to validate latency on a mirrored subset of traffic (500 RPS target).

Attachments in this thread: Mercator_MOU_v2.pdf, pricing_summary_commit_increase.pdf.

If that looks good I can loop in Finance/legal to draft a short MOU. Friday 2pm PT works — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: pricing_summary_commit_increase.pdf (2 pages)

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@mercatorretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Elise Thompson <elise@mercatorretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Need options for committed throughput increase ahead of Q4 holiday

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the clear options. A couple procurement/legal asks before we move to MOU: 
1) Can you confirm the exact overage rate if we exceed the 2.4B in a month? We need a cap for budgeting (we typically ask vendors to cap overages or provide an emergency credit line).
2) For the soft-throttle window, can you define the latency SLO degradation policy (e.g., warning thresholds, mitigation steps) so our SREs can align runbooks?
3) We typically ask for a 45-day termination window on pilots if they materially impact availability. Is that acceptable?

Laura — looping in the Redwood AM to help with timelines and to capture any product caveats.

Regards,
Rajiv
VP, Infrastructure
Mercator Retail

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elise Thompson <elise@mercatorretail.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@mercatorretail.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Need options for committed throughput increase ahead of Q4 holiday

Elise / Rajiv —

Thanks for the questions — quick responses and next steps: 
1) Overage rate: overage will bill at the existing burst rate (no surprise uplift). For budgeting comfort we can include a temporary overage cap at 25% above the commit for the first two billing cycles, after which standard overage terms apply. We’ll put that cap in the MOU invoice appendix.
2) Soft-throttle SLOs: we will configure a three-tier warning system —
   - Warning 1 (80% of burst pocket): automated email to Mercator SREs, no throttling, escalates to Redwood on-call.
   - Warning 2 (95%): soft-throttle begins for non-critical endpoints (background batch requests), latency SLO target relaxed by up to 15% for those paths.
   - Hard-throttle (100%+ beyond cap): strict rate limiting for excess RPS; emergency credit path available on exec approval.
   Documentation and runbook snippets will be appended to the MOU.
3) Pilot termination window: 45 days is acceptable for the pilot clause; we will add a mutually-agreed remediation period before termination rights can be exercised.

Next steps / timeline:
- I’ll prepare an MOU draft (Mercator_MOU_v2.pdf) that includes the 25% emergency cap for first two cycles, SLO runbook summary, and the pilot termination clause.
- Jonas to follow up with draft invoice and calendar invite for the call Friday at 2pm PT.
- Post-call: sign MOU via DocuSign and open a provisioning ticket to reserve autoscale capacity for Sept.

Elise — any product caveats on your side we should bake into the runbook?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Mercator_MOU_v2.pdf (MOU draft)
